key_insight: GeoThinker shifts 3D geometry use in MLLMs from passive global fusion to active, task-driven perception—letting the model query and align geometric information selectively to reduce semantic-geometry misalignment and redundant signals.
problem_solved: Existing approaches fuse global geometric priors indiscriminately, causing semantic-geometry misalignment, noise, and inefficiency for spatial reasoning tasks in multimodal LLMs.
method: Active perception controller: the model issues targeted geometry queries (e.g., locations, viewpoints, primitives) instead of ingesting a monolithic geometry stream.
Localized geometry encoding + alignment: the 3D encoder returns task-relevant, localized geometric features that are selectively aligned with language semantics rather than blindly mixed.
Iterative feedback loop: language-driven queries guide further geometric sampling/attention, forming a closed-loop integration that improves relevance and reduces redundancy.
impact: By integrating geometry actively, GeoThinker improves spatial reasoning accuracy and efficiency, making MLLMs more reliable for 3D-aware tasks (e.g., navigation, manipulation, scene understanding) while reducing unnecessary compute and noisy signals.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: passive global fusion vs GeoThinker active-query pipeline to illustrate the paradigm shift.
End-to-end pipeline flowchart: language query → geometry query → localized encoding → alignment → answer, showing the feedback loop.
Point-cloud / attention overlay: example scene with highlighted queried regions vs ignored geometry to show selective perception.
Bar/line chart: comparative metrics (accuracy, latency, redundancy) for passive baseline vs GeoThinker.
paper_title: Thinking with Geometry: Active Geometry Integration for Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Tao Tang, Kun Xiang, Zihan Guo
